title: 1982 AHSME Problem 14
statement: In the adjoining figure, points \(B\) and \(C\) lie on line segment \(AD,\) and \(AB,\) \(BC,\) and \(CD\) are diameters of circles \(O,\) \(N,\) and \(P,\) respectively. Circles \(O,\) \(N,\) and \(P\) all have radius \(15,\) and the line \(AG\) is tangent to circle \(P\) at \(G.\) If \(AG\) intersects circle \(N\) at points \(E\) and \(F,\) then chord \(EF\) has length

solutions.text:
Here \(AP=75,\) \(PG=15,\) and \(AG\perp PG.\) The distance from \(N\) to \(AG\) scales with \(\frac{AN}{AP}=\frac{45}{75},\) so it is \(15(\frac{45}{75})=9.\) Therefore the chord in the radius-\(15\) circle has length \(2\sqrt{15^2-9^2}=2\sqrt{144}=24.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Use right triangle \(APG\) to find the distance from \(N\) to line \(AG\)
A chord at distance \(d\) from a circle’s center has length \(2\sqrt{r^2-d^2}\)
